* Overview

Komorebi is a tiling window manager for Windows 11 written in Rust. It runs as
a background process and manages window placement, workspaces, and focus from
=komorebic= CLI commands.

All hotkeys are dispatched by [[https://github.com/jtroo/kanata][Kanata]], so no separate WHKD or AHK daemon runs at
startup.

Started with: =komorebic start --ffm --bar= (follow-focus mode + status bar; no =--whkd=).

This config covers: layout algorithm and padding, window borders, hide/move behaviour,
and per-application ignore/manage rules. Per-app float/manage overrides live in the
companion =applications.json= referenced below.

* Core Configuration

** Paths and Behaviour

=app_specific_configuration_path= points Komorebi at the per-app rules file.
=Cloak= hides windows by cloaking them (invisible but still in the process tree),
which is more reliable than =Hide= on Windows 11 — =Hide= can cause some apps to
fully suspend. =Insert= for cross-monitor moves places the window into the target
monitor's BSP tree rather than swapping it with the current occupant.
Zero padding produces a full-bleed tiling layout; increase values here or per-workspace
for spacing.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "app_specific_configuration_path": "$Env:USERPROFILE/.config/komorebi/applications.json",
  "window_hiding_behaviour": "Cloak",
  "cross_monitor_move_behaviour": "Insert",
  "default_workspace_padding": 0,
  "default_container_padding": 0,
#+end_src

** Border Configuration

A 5px border on the active window provides visual focus feedback without affecting window
geometry. =border_offset: -1= draws the border inside the window frame rather than
outside it, so the border doesn't alter window geometry or leave pixel gaps between
tiles.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "border": true,
  "border_width": 5,
  "border_offset": -1,
#+end_src

* Window Rules

Komorebi automatically manages most windows. Rules here carve out exceptions in two
directions: ignore (exclude from tiling entirely), *floating* (still managed on the
current workspace but never forced into BSP tiles), and manage (force-include windows
that Komorebi would otherwise skip).

Exe matching with =Equals= is *case-sensitive*. If Copilot still tiles despite
=mscopilot.exe=, Windows may be reporting a different exe casing — use a
=Regex= rule with =(?i)= for case-insensitive matching.

** Ignore Rules

Windows in this list are excluded from tiling and float freely above the managed grid.

- =QuakeTerm= — WezTerm quake terminal (managed separately). Ignored by window
  class so regular =wezterm-gui.exe= instances still tile normally on the ops
  workspace.
- =MSCTFIME UI= / =Default IME= — Windows text input service windows. These are
  invisible system-level popups; tiling them breaks input.
- Microsoft Copilot host (=mscopilot.exe=, often Chromium / =Chrome_WidgetWin_1=),
  plus =Regex= =(?i)mscopilot\\.exe= so casing from the OS cannot bypass the rule.
- =ApplicationFrameHost.exe= whose title contains =Copilot= — alternate shell for the
  pinned/desktop Copilot window when it does not report as =mscopilot.exe=.
- =Qt\\d+QWindow.*Tool.*= + =qutebrowser.exe= — qutebrowser Qt auxiliary tooltip/tool window (hovering tabs, links, UI). Compound rule in =ignore_rules= excludes it
  from management entirely (unlike floating, which still battles the layout).
- =Qt\\d+QWindow.*Tool.*= (standalone, no Exe guard) — catch any Qt tooltip
  windows that slip through or come from helper processes. Added as a standalone
  class-based rule so it does not require the =qutebrowser.exe= Exe match.
- =Phoneme Live Preview= — =phoneme-tray.exe= live transcription overlay.
- =Phoneme Recording Indicator= — =phoneme-tray.exe= recording indicator overlay.
  Both ignored by title (not Exe) so the main =Phoneme= window still tiles.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "ignore_rules": [

    },

      "matching_strategy": "Equals"

    {

** Floating applications

Windows that should stay on the current workspace but never be forced into BSP
tiles. Typically dialog boxes, floating toolbars, and context menus.

- **Copilot**: Chromium/Electron surface — if *ignore* rules still fail.
- **qutebrowser context menu**: Qt6 popup (=Qt\\d+QWindowPopup.*=)
  created by right-clicking on a page. The title is always "qutebrowser" and
  the class is the Qt6 popup window class matched with a version-tolerant regex. Without this rule, Komorebi
  tiles the popup as if it were a full browser window.
  - Diagnosed with =komorebic visible-windows= while the context menu was visible
  - The class name embeds the Qt version (for example 6.11.0 → =Qt6110=), so the rule uses =Regex= instead of an exact versioned class
  - The main qutebrowser window uses =Qt6110QWindowIcon= — any other qutebrowser
    window class is likely a popup or child window
- **qutebrowser tooltip**: Qt6 tooltip (=Qt\\d+QWindow.*Tool.*=)
  spawned when hovering over tabs, links, or UI elements. Same diagnostic method:
  =komorebic visible-windows= while a tooltip is visible.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "floating_applications": [
    {
      "kind": "Exe",
      "id": "(?i)^mscopilot\\.exe$",
      "matching_strategy": "Regex"
    },
    [
      {
        "kind": "Exe",
        "id": "mscopilot.exe",
        "matching_strategy": "Equals"
      },
      {
        "kind": "Class",
        "id": "Chrome_WidgetWin_1",
        "matching_strategy": "Equals"
      }
    ],
    [
      {
        "kind": "Exe",
        "id": "qutebrowser.exe",
        "matching_strategy": "Equals"
      },
      {
        "kind": "Class",
        "id": "Qt\\d+QWindowPopup.*",
        "matching_strategy": "Regex"
      }
    ]
  ],
#+end_src

** Manage Rules

Some windows are not detected as manageable by default — typically UWP apps hosted
in =ApplicationFrameHost.exe= and Electron apps with non-standard window styles.
These rules force Komorebi to tile them.

- =qutebrowser.exe= — explicitly managed so =remove_titlebar_applications= and
  =initial_workspace_rules= apply reliably.
- =claude.exe= — the Claude desktop app (Electron). Komorebi sometimes skips Electron
  windows; explicit manage ensures it's always tiled.
- =ApplicationFrameHost + Claude= — some UWP/hosted Claude windows show up under
  ApplicationFrameHost; the compound rule catches them by title.


#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "manage_rules": [

    {
      "kind": "Exe",
      "id": "qutebrowser.exe",
      "matching_strategy": "Equals"
    },
    {
      "kind": "Exe",
      "id": "claude.exe",
      "matching_strategy": "Equals"
    },
    [
      {
        "kind": "Exe",
        "id": "ApplicationFrameHost.exe",
        "matching_strategy": "Equals"
      },
      {
        "kind": "Title",
        "id": "Claude",
        "matching_strategy": "Contains"
      }
    ]
  ],
#+end_src

** Remove Title Bar

Windows that should not have title bars or window frames. Komorebi strips the
non-client area (title bar + borders) and draws its own border instead.

- =qutebrowser.exe= — title bar removed; border drawn by Komorebi.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "remove_titlebar_applications": [
    {
      "kind": "Exe",
      "id": "qutebrowser.exe",
      "matching_strategy": "Equals"
    }
  ],
#+end_src

** Layered Applications

Apps that use layered/transparent windows and need special compositing handling.
Without this, borders and transparency effects can glitch on these windows.
Currently only =Cursor.exe= is listed. Copilot uses =ignore_rules= and
=floating_applications= (see above), not layered compositing.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json


  "layered_applications": [
    {
      "kind": "Exe",
      "id": "Cursor.exe",
      "matching_strategy": "Equals"
    }
  ],
#+end_src

* Theme

Catppuccin Mocha palette wired into Komorebi's border and stackbar colours.
Each border role is assigned a named Catppuccin colour so the UI stays cohesive
with the rest of the desktop.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "theme": {
    "palette": "Catppuccin",
    "name": "Mocha",
    "single_border": "Pink",
    "stack_border": "Sky",
    "monocle_border": "Mauve",
    "floating_border": "Sapphire",
    "unfocused_border": "Surface1",
    "unfocused_locked_border": "Peach",
    "stackbar_background": "Surface0",
    "stackbar_focused_text": "Teal",
    "stackbar_unfocused_text": "Overlay0",
    "bar_accent": "Pink"
  },
#+end_src

* Animations

Window movement animations make workspace/focus transitions feel smoother.
Enabled with =EaseOutSine= easing at 60fps over 250ms. This is experimental —
minor visual artifacts may appear during rapid tiling changes.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json
  "animation": {
    "enabled": false,
    "duration": 100,
    "fps": 240,
    "style": {
      "movement": "Linear",
      "transparency": "Linear"
    }
  },
#+end_src

* Monitors

Bottom monitor (1920×1200): seven named workspaces (four Grid + three scrolling): browse, write, emacs, ops, cowork (scrolling, 2 col), social (scrolling, 2 col), focus (scrolling, 1 col).
Top monitor (2560×1440): seven BSP workspaces (browse, write, emacs, ops, cowork, social, focus). The top monitor follows
the bottom: =LAlt+N= switches workspaces on the *current* monitor only;
=Shift+LAlt+N= switches both monitors simultaneously via =focus-workspaces N=.

*Initial workspace rules* on the bottom monitor route a fixed set of apps at launch
(Firefox, qutebrowser, Obsidian, main - emacs, FIXME: no rule found for VS Code,
Claude, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity, Open Code, terminals, social stack, phoneme). Copilot is
*not* auto-routed—open it on whatever workspace you are on.
No =initial_workspace_rules= on the top monitor — apps launched there stay there
but can be moved to the bottom monitor with =LAlt+Space=.

Switch any workspace at runtime with =komorebic change-layout <layout>=.

#+begin_src json :tangle komorebi.json

* Bar Configuration

=komorebi-bar= is a standalone status bar companion to Komorebi. It reads
workspace and layout state from Komorebi over a named pipe and renders a
Catppuccin-themed bar at the top of each monitor.

Both monitors get their own bar. The bottom bar uses =komorebi.bar.json= (monitor 0),
the top bar uses =komorebi.bar.top.json= (monitor 1). Each bar is started via the
=--config= flag:
: komorebic bar --config "%USERPROFILE%\.config\komorebi\komorebi.bar.json"
: komorebic bar --config "%USERPROFILE%\.config\komorebi\komorebi.bar.top.json"

Bars are 32 px tall — the same value referenced as =VerticalOffset= in
=wtq.jsonc= and =toggle-komorebi-bar.ps1= (30 px offset leaves 2 px overlap for clean
edge rendering). Toggling the bar with =LAlt+b= (via =toggle-komorebi-bar.ps1=) stops
or starts both =komorebi-bar.exe= instances and restarts Komorebi and WTQ so each tool
recalculates the work area with the new bar height.

=transparency_alpha= at 235/255 (~92%) gives a slightly frosted look that
matches the WTQ terminal opacity (90%).

** Left Widgets

Two Komorebi-specific widgets displayed on the left:

| Widget             | Shows                                                    |
|--------------------+----------------------------------------------------------|
| =workspaces=       | Layout name + workspace dots (filled = active)            |
| =focused_window=   | Currently focused window title and application icon       |

=hide_empty_workspaces= is false so all seven dots are always visible, giving
a stable visual reference for workspace position.

** Right Widgets

System metrics on the right. =Storage= is disabled — disk usage rarely needs
monitoring during normal work. Re-enable by setting =enable: true= if needed.

| Widget    | Shows                                   |
|-----------+-----------------------------------------|
| =Update=  | Pending system updates indicator        |
| =Media=   | Now-playing artist and track title      |
| =Storage= | Disk usage (disabled)                   |
| =Cpu=     | CPU usage percentage                    |
| =Memory=  | RAM usage percentage                    |

** Full Bar Config

* Known Issues

** tangle-fallback.ps1 ignores =#+PROPERTY:= default =:tangle=

The =tangle-fallback.ps1= script (used because Emacs 30.2 batch-mode org-babel-
tangle is broken for this file) matches only explicit =:tangle TARGET= on
=#+begin_src= lines.  It does /not/ inherit the buffer-level default from:

  #+PROPERTY: header-args:json :tangle komorebi.json

This was discovered on 2026-05-24 when the context menu floating rule was added
but did not appear in the tangled output.  To fix, every =#+begin_src json=
block that should go into =komorebi.json= must have an explicit
=:tangle komorebi.json= on its =#+begin_src= line (even though it duplicates
the PROPERTY default).  The bar config block has its own
=:tangle komorebi.bar.json= and is unaffected.
